source.highlight: Footballers donate socks to hooves in need
source.after: The U.K. football club Arsenal have donated dozens of socks — to a donkey and horse sanctuary. … The soccer socks can act as a compression sleeve and hold bandages in place and protect them from flies.

source.highlight: A rare family of barn owls moved into Manhattan's Upper West Side. New Yorkers are captivated
source.after: Manhattan's Upper West Side has been reveling in the company of its latest celebrities: A family of barn owls nested in a water tower atop a building near Central Park. This is the first documented instance of barn owls nesting in Manhattan in modern history, according to one expert, and the owls have attracted nightly crowds of people in the street eager to get a glimpse of the elusive birds.

source.highlight: The true fake story behind the annual Virginia City Camel Race
source.after: Back in the 1950s, a newspaper editor in Nevada wrote a fake story about a camel race happening in his town as a joke. Eventually, he helped make it a real thing and the annual Virginia City Camel Race was born, which continues to this day.

source.before: It was the 50th time that the race has run through all five boroughs of the city.
source.highlight: There were just over 2,000 competitors in 1976, the seventh running of the race, including only 88 women. About 60,000 runners stepped up to the starting line Sunday, with nearly half of them women.
source.after: There were runners from more than 140 countries competing Sunday, including defending men's Kipruto.

source.before: Falkner, the Princeton researcher, says humans can also learn physical skills by watching others, like in sports.
source.highlight: FALKNER: The question is not whether you can be a professional athlete by watching the NFL, but are you better at football for watching sports than if you had never watched anything? And the answer is absolutely yes.
